questions.subject: STATISTICS
questions.learningObjective: State when a paired t test is invalid
questions.stem: Explain when a paired t test on before-after differences is inappropriate.

answer.exemplar: A paired t test is inappropriate when differences are severely non-normal with small samples, or when observations are not truly paired, because the mean difference then lacks a valid sampling distribution.

questions.explanation: The paired t test assumes paired, approximately normal differences. Non-paired units or severe non-normality undermine validity.
questions.hint: Check pairing and normality of differences.

questions.learningObjective: Explain why pairing reduces variability
questions.stem: Explain why a paired comparison can detect smaller differences than an independent one.

answer.exemplar: Pairing removes between-unit variability by comparing each unit to itself, so the remaining difference variability is smaller and smaller true differences become detectable.

questions.explanation: Pairing controls for unit-level differences. The reduced variability in differences increases sensitivity to condition effects.
questions.hint: Pairing removes between-unit variability.
